title: House of Jagiellon
capsule: As the ruling dynasty rather than the state, the House of Jagiellon in this 1450–1572 window held the thrones of Poland and Lithuania — and intermittently Bohemia and Hungary — from Casimir IV (r. 1447–1492) through his sons, down to Sigismund II Augustus, whose childless death in 1572 ended the dynasty and, with it, hereditary succession in the Polish-Lithuanian union.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Jagiellonian territorial extent is well attested from royal charters, diet records, and ecclesiastical sources for Poland and Lithuania; Bohemian and Hungarian holdings are documented but the dataset geometry for the composite state carries moderate spatial uncertainty at frontiers. Capsule researched for this polity/era specifically (confidence: high).
